p: Many students find it hard to learn English. They think grammar is too difficult and words are too many.
But successful learners have one thing in common: they practice a little every day. Ten minutes of reading is better than two hours once a week.
So do not wait for a free weekend. Start with what you have today.
q: What do successful English learners have in common?
o: They practice a little every day.
ex: 第二段明确指出 successful learners have one thing in common: they practice a little every day（成功的学习者有一个共同点：他们每天都练习一点点）。其余选项在文中都没有依据。

p: Sleep is important for students. Studies show that students who sleep less than six hours do worse in tests.
The reason is simple. During sleep, the brain stores what you learned during the day.
So if you want to remember new words, a good night's sleep may help more than another hour of study.
q: What happens during sleep according to the passage?
o: The brain stores what you learned.
ex: 第三句直接说明 During sleep, the brain stores what you learned during the day（睡眠期间，大脑会储存你白天学到的东西）。A 项与原文矛盾（大脑并非完全休息）。

p: More and more young people in China are choosing to exercise after work. Gyms in big cities are now full in the evening.
One reason is health. Long hours of sitting in front of a computer make people feel tired and stiff. Exercise helps them relax.
Another reason is social. For many young workers, the gym is a place to meet friends, not just to keep fit.
However, experts warn that people should choose exercise that suits their own body, not just follow what is popular.
q: What do experts warn people about?
o: Going to the gym at night.
ex: 最后一段 experts warn that people should choose exercise that suits their own body（专家提醒人们应该选择适合自己身体的运动），对应 B。

p: Online shopping has changed the way people buy things. Today you can order almost anything with a phone.
The biggest advantage is convenience. You do not need to leave home, and prices are often lower than in shops.
But there is a problem: you cannot touch or try the product before you buy it. Sometimes what you get is not what you saw on the screen.
Many companies are now trying to solve this by offering free returns.
q: What is the main problem of online shopping mentioned?
o: You cannot check the product before buying.
It takes too long to deliver.
ex: 第三段指出 But there is a problem: you cannot touch or try the product before you buy it（但你无法在购买前触摸或试用商品），即 B。A 与原文相反（网上价格通常更低）。

p: Reading is a habit that is easy to lose. Many people say they have no time, but they spend hours on short videos.
The truth is that short videos give quick pleasure, while books give slow but deeper satisfaction.
A simple way to start is to keep a book where you can see it, such as on your desk or beside your bed. Out of sight, out of mind.
Set a small goal, like five pages a day. Small habits grow into big changes.
q: What does the author suggest doing to start reading?
ex: 第三段建议 keep a book where you can see it（把书放在看得见的地方），即 B。D 项偷换了数量单位，原文是 five pages（五页）而非 five books。

p: When companies hire new workers, they often value attitude over experience. A person who is willing to learn can grow quickly, while a person with a fixed mind may stop improving.
This does not mean experience is useless. It means that in fast-changing industries, the ability to keep learning matters more than what you already know.
For students, the message is clear: do not be afraid of what you do not know. Be afraid of refusing to learn it.
q: What does the passage say about experience?
o: It is more important than attitude.
It matters less than the ability to learn.
It is required by all companies.
ex: 第二段说明 the ability to keep learning matters more than what you already know（持续学习的能力比你已经掌握的知识更重要），即经验不如学习能力重要，选 C。B 项过于绝对，原文说 It means experience is not useless。

p: Every morning, Li Hua gets up at six and reads English aloud for twenty minutes. He says the morning is the quietest time of the day.
His roommate prefers to study at night. Both of them pass their exams, so there is no single best time to study.
q: When does Li Hua read English aloud?
ex: 第一段说 Every morning ... reads English aloud for twenty minutes（每天早上大声读英语二十分钟），所以选 B。室友喜欢晚上学习，那是室友的习惯，不是李华的。

p: Do not try to learn fifty new words in one day. Most of them will be gone by tomorrow. Fifteen words a day is a better plan.
The important thing is to meet the same word again and again. Your memory needs repetition more than speed.
q: What does the writer say your memory needs most?
ex: 第二段说 Your memory needs repetition more than speed（记忆需要的是重复，而不是速度），直接对上 C。B 项在文中没有依据。

p: Spring in this city is short. It often rains, and the temperature goes up and down. Many people catch cold in April.
Summer comes quickly in May. By June, the afternoons are hot and wet, and most people stay inside.
q: Why do many people catch cold in April?
o: Because the temperature changes a lot.
ex: 第一段先给出 temperature goes up and down（气温忽高忽低），紧接着就说很多人四月感冒，两者是因果关系，选 B。A 项说「每天下雨」过于绝对，原文只说 often rains。

p: A man went to buy a coat. The shop had two kinds: one for two hundred yuan and one for six hundred.
He chose the cheaper one. Three weeks later the zip broke, and he had to buy another coat. The cheap coat cost him more in the end.
q: What is the lesson of the story?
o: A low price is not always the lowest cost.
He should not have bought a coat.
ex: 末句 The cheap coat cost him more in the end（便宜外套最后让他花得更多）说明价格低不等于总花费低，选 B。A 项「便宜的东西总是差的」过于绝对，原文只讲了一个例子。

p: Sitting for a long time is bad for your back. Many office workers feel pain after a few years.
Doctors suggest standing up every hour. Even two minutes of walking helps. You do not need a long exercise to make a difference.
q: What do doctors suggest?
o: Running for an hour every day.
ex: 第二段第一句 Doctors suggest standing up every hour（医生建议每小时站起来一次），选 B。C 项「换把好椅子」文中没提。

p: The bus to the airport takes about fifty minutes. The underground takes thirty, but you have to change trains once.
A taxi is the fastest, but it costs five times more. Most students choose the underground.
q: Why do most students take the underground?
ex: 出租车最快但贵五倍，公交慢，地铁比出租车便宜又比公交快，所以学生选地铁，选 C。A 项是出租车的特征，不是地铁的。

p: Our neighbourhood started a recycling programme last year. Each family got three boxes: one for paper, one for plastic and one for other waste.
At first many people were confused. Now almost everyone sorts the waste without thinking about it.
q: What happened after the programme started?
o: People slowly got used to sorting waste.
ex: 第二段 At first many people were confused. Now almost everyone sorts the waste without thinking（一开始困惑，现在几乎人人下意识地分类），正是「慢慢习惯」的意思，选 B。

p: Tom and Jack were neighbours but had never spoken. One evening Tom's water pipe broke and water ran into the corridor.
Jack knocked on his door and helped him fix it. Since then they have had dinner together every month.
q: What brought the two neighbours together?
ex: 第二段说 Jack ... helped him fix it，起因就是水管破了，选 B。文中完全没有提到爱好、聚会或球赛。

p: The library closes at ten at night. Many students stay until the last minute.
The staff say the busiest hour is nine, when people suddenly remember their deadlines. Some of them only start working at nine.
q: What does the staff say about the hour before closing?
ex: 第二段 the busiest hour is nine，而九点正是闭馆前一小时，选 B。A 项把「最忙」错记成了「最安静」。

p: A study asked two hundred students how often they check their phones. The average answer was once every twelve minutes.
The same students believed they checked only three or four times an hour. Most people are not aware of their own habits.
q: What did the study find?
o: Students check their phones less than they think.
Students check their phones more often than they think.
Students only use phones for study.
ex: 每十二分钟一次约等于每小时五次，比学生自己估计的三到四次更频繁，所以是「比以为的更频繁」，选 B。

p: My grandmother has cooked for our family for forty years. She never uses a written recipe.
When I asked her to write one down, she laughed and said the amount depends on the day. Cooking, for her, is a feeling.
q: Why does the grandmother not write down her recipes?
o: She thinks the amount changes each day.
She wants to keep them secret.
ex: 奶奶说 the amount depends on the day（分量要看当天情况），所以写不下来，选 B。A 项说她不会写字，文中没有任何依据。

p: Wang Lin works in a small company. He arrives fifteen minutes early every day.
His manager noticed. Last month, when a new team needed a leader, the manager chose him. Being on time is not a small thing.
q: Why did the manager choose Wang Lin?
ex: 第二段先说他每天早到十五分钟，再说经理因此选他，最后一句点明主题，选 B。A、C 两项文中都没提。

p: The old town has narrow stone streets. Cars are not allowed, so you have to walk.
That is exactly why people like it. Without cars, the streets are quiet, and you can hear the water running beside the houses.
q: Why do people like the old town?
o: Because it is near the sea.
ex: 第二段 Without cars, the streets are quiet（没有车，街道才安静），这正是人们喜欢它的原因，选 B。A 项与原文 narrow streets 相反。

p: Many students eat only two meals a day and skip breakfast. They often feel sleepy in the second class.
A small breakfast makes a big difference. Bread, an egg and some milk are enough to keep the morning going.
q: What is the passage mainly about?
ex: 全文围绕「不吃早餐会犯困」和「吃一点早餐就有用」展开，主题是早餐的重要性，选 B。A 项只讲到食物名称，不是主旨。

p: Rain water is collected on the roof of our building. Pipes carry it down to a tank.
We use it to water the plants in the yard. Last summer we did not need the tap water once.
q: What is the rain water used for?
ex: 第二段 We use it to water the plants in the yard（用来浇院子里的植物），选 C。A 项「饮用」在文中没有出现。

p: There is a small park between two tall buildings in our area. It is only about twenty metres across.
But at seven in the evening it is full: children playing, old people walking, and young people talking. Small places can hold a lot of life.
q: What does the writer think about the small park?
o: It is too small to be useful.
It is well used by the neighbours.
ex: 第二段描写傍晚公园里满是小孩、老人和年轻人，最后一句说小地方也能承载很多生活，说明它被邻居们充分利用，选 B。

p: When you read in English, do not stop at every new word. Try to finish the sentence first.
Often the next sentence explains the word. If it still does not make sense, then look it up.
q: What should you do when you meet a new word?
ex: 第一段 do not stop at every new word. Try to finish the sentence first，选 B。A 项正是作者劝你不要做的事。

p: High speed trains have changed the way people travel. A trip of six hours by car now takes two.
Many people work in one city and visit their family in another. The distance has not changed, but the time has.
q: What has changed according to the passage?
ex: 最后一句直接点明 The distance has not changed, but the time has（距离没变，时间变了），选 B。A 项恰好是作者说「没变」的东西。

p: Every Sunday, a group of students cleans the river bank near the school.
Their teacher says the aim is not only to clean the river. It is to help the students notice the world around them.
q: What is the teacher's aim?
o: To help students notice the world.
ex: 第二段 It is to help the students notice the world around them，选 B。第一段也说了清理河流只是手段之一（not only）。

p: Before an exam, many students cannot sleep. They keep thinking about what they have not learned.
A teacher gave simple advice: write down three things you do know. Then you will remember that you are not starting from zero.
q: What did the teacher advise?
o: To write down three things you know.
ex: 第二段给出建议 write down three things you do know（写下三件你已经会的事），选 B。A 项恰是作者要解决的问题，不是建议。

p: In the north, families often make dumplings together on New Year's Eve. Everyone has a job.
The grandmother makes the filling, the parents roll the skins and the children fold. Talking while working is half the fun.
q: According to the passage, what is half the fun?
ex: 末句 Talking while working is half the fun（边做边聊是一半的乐趣），选 B。文中没有提到买肉或奖品。

p: A student asked his teacher how to improve his writing. The teacher told him to read more, not write more.
He was surprised. But after three months of reading a little every day, his sentences became longer and clearer.
q: What did the teacher tell the student to do?
ex: 第一段 The teacher told him to read more, not write more，选 B。A 项是学生原本以为该做的，正是被老师否掉的那个。

p: Learning to cook is cheaper than eating out. A simple meal at home costs a quarter of the price.
It is also healthier, because you decide how much oil and salt goes in. The only cost is your time.
q: What is the only real cost of cooking at home?
ex: 最后一句 The only cost is your time（唯一的代价是你的时间），选 C。文中明确说在家做饭更便宜，所以 A 项不对。

p: Old people often find smartphones difficult. The words on the screen are small, and the menus change with every update.
Some companies now make phones with big buttons and only three functions: call, message and camera. That is enough for most users.
q: Why are the new phones easier for old people?
o: They have big buttons and few functions.
ex: 第二段 big buttons and three simple functions（大按钮、只有三个简单功能），选 B。文中没有提到价格或重量。

p: A cloth bag can be used more than a thousand times. A plastic bag is usually used once.
If one person uses a cloth bag for a year, that is about three hundred plastic bags that are not thrown away.
q: How many plastic bags can one cloth bag replace in a year?
ex: 第二段 about three hundred plastic bags（大约三百个塑料袋），选 B。C 项是「一千次」的误记，那是布袋能用多少次，不是一年的减量。

p: The English corner meets every Wednesday. Anyone can come, and no one is forced to speak.
The rule is simple: speak English, and do not laugh at others. Most new members speak within ten minutes.
q: What is the rule of the English corner?
o: Everyone must speak for ten minutes.
Speak English and do not laugh at others.
ex: 第二段 The rule is simple: speak English, and do not laugh at others，选 B。A 项混淆了「十分钟内就会开口」这句事实。

p: Walking thirty minutes a day is enough exercise for most people. It is safe for the knees and needs no equipment.
The hard part is not the walking. It is deciding to go out of the door. Once you are outside, the rest is easy.
q: What is the hard part according to the passage?
ex: 第二段 The hard part is not the walking. It is deciding to go out of the door，选 C。作者明确排除了「走路本身难」这个选项。

p: A woman kept a small notebook of words she heard but did not know. She wrote them down and looked them up at night.
After one year she had twelve hundred words. She said the notebook taught her more than any class.
q: How many words did she collect in a year?
ex: 第二段 she had twelve hundred words（一千二百个词），选 B。D 项多了一个零，是一万二千。

p: When Chen Wei started university, he was surprised by how much free time he had. Nobody told him when to study or when to sleep.
For the first month he did very little. Then his first test result arrived, and it was far below what he expected.
He began making a simple plan: three hours of study a day, and no phone until they were finished. It was not a clever plan, but it worked.
q: What made Chen Wei change his habits?
ex: 第二段说他的第一次考试成绩 far below what he expected（远低于预期），第三段他才开始做计划，所以触发点是成绩，选 B。老师、父母、朋友在文中都没有出现。

p: Shared bicycles appeared in Chinese cities about ten years ago. The idea was simple: you find a bike with your phone, ride it, and leave it anywhere.
At first the streets were full of broken bikes, and some people complained. Most of that has since been cleared up by the companies themselves.
Riders say the best part is the price. A short trip costs less than a bus ticket and takes half the time.
q: What do riders like most about shared bicycles?
ex: 第三段 Riders say the best part is the price（乘客说最棒的是价格），并接着说比公交便宜、时间少一半，所以是价格和速度，选 B。

p: Li Fang's first job was in a large company. On her first day she was given a desk, a computer and nothing else.
For two weeks she asked a different colleague one question every morning. By the end of the month she knew who handled what.
When a new worker joined three months later, Li Fang was the one who showed her around.
q: How did Li Fang learn about the company?
ex: 第二段 For two weeks she asked a different colleague one question every morning，选 B。A 项的「手册」文中没有提到，反而强调公司什么都没给她。

p: Many people cannot fall asleep because they look at a screen until they switch off the light. The light from a phone tells the brain that it is still daytime.
The effect is strongest in the last hour before bed. Doctors therefore suggest putting the phone in another room, not just on the bedside table.
People who try this often report that they fall asleep faster within a week.
q: What do doctors suggest?
o: Leaving the phone outside the bedroom.
ex: 第二段说 putting the phone in another room, not just on the bedside table（把手机放到另一个房间，而不只是放床头柜），选 C。A 项「调暗屏幕」是原文没有的建议。

p: Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic reach the sea. Most of it does not come from ships but from the land, carried down by rivers.
Sun and waves break the plastic into very small pieces. Fish eat these pieces, and the plastic then enters the food chain.
Scientists say the cheapest solution is to stop the waste before it reaches the river.
q: Where does most sea plastic come from?
ex: 第一段 Most of it does not come from ships but from the land, carried down by rivers，作者特意排除了「船」这个常见误解，选 B。

p: Some schools have stopped giving homework to young children. The reason is that homework in the early years is often just more of the same classwork.
Instead, the schools ask children to read with a parent for twenty minutes a day. Reading together also gives the family a quiet time in the evening.
Results so far have been good, and many parents say their evenings are calmer.
q: What do these schools ask children to do instead of homework?
ex: 第二段 Instead, the schools ask children to read with a parent for twenty minutes a day，选 B。D 项「做更多练习」正是被取消的东西。

p: Most people worry about their phone being stolen, but the greater risk is invisible. Apps collect information about where you go and what you buy.
The information is often used to show you advertisements. That is not a crime, but it means someone is watching all day long.
Reading the permission list when you install an app takes only a minute.
q: What is the greater risk mentioned in the passage?
ex: 第一段 the greater risk is invisible. Apps collect information about where you go and what you buy，选 C。A 项是作者对比出来的、相对小的风险。

p: A family in Shanghai tried an experiment: for one month they bought nothing except food and medicine.
The first week was difficult because the habit of buying was stronger than the need. After that the family found they did not miss the things they used to buy.
At the end of the month they had saved enough for a short holiday.
q: What was difficult in the first week?
ex: 第二段 The first week was difficult because the habit of buying was stronger than the need（习惯比需要更强），选 B。

p: In some cultures, a gift is opened in front of the person who gave it. In others, it is put aside and opened later.
Neither way is more polite. The first shows interest and the second avoids putting the giver under pressure.
Travellers are advised to watch what the people around them do.
q: What does the writer advise travellers to do?
ex: 最后一句 Travellers are advised to watch what the people around them do，选 C。文中明确说两种方式都礼貌，所以 A 项不成立。

p: Students who write notes by hand often remember more than those who type them. The reason is not the pen itself.
Writing by hand forces you to choose what matters, because you cannot write everything. Typing lets you copy every word without deciding anything.
The choosing is what makes the memory stay.
q: Why does handwriting help memory?
o: Because it forces you to choose what matters.
Because pens are better than keyboards.
ex: 第二段 Writing by hand forces you to choose what matters，第三段又说 The choosing is what makes the memory stay，选 B。

p: More young people in big cities now live alone. Some chose it, and some simply have no choice because of work.
Studies find that people who live alone often cook less and eat out more. They also sleep at less regular hours.
But the same studies show no clear difference in how happy they feel.
q: What do the studies find about people who live alone?
o: They cook less and sleep less regularly.
ex: 第二段说他们 cook less and eat out more、sleep at less regular hours，第三段明确说 happiness 没有明显差别，所以排除 A、选 B。

p: Travelling alone sounds lonely, but many people try it at least once. The first two days are usually the hardest.
You have to make every small decision, from where to eat to which bus to take. There is nobody to blame when it goes wrong.
Most travellers describe the third day as the point where they begin to enjoy it.
q: What do most solo travellers say about the third day?
o: They begin to enjoy the trip.
ex: 最后一句 Most travellers describe the third day as the point where they begin to enjoy it，选 B。

p: My grandfather learned to use a smartphone at eighty. He now sends me a voice message every morning.
At first the family worried that he would spend all day on the screen. In fact he uses it for two things only: messages and the weather.
The messages are usually about the weather.
q: How does the grandfather use his phone?
ex: 第二段 he uses it for two things only: messages and the weather，选 B。A、C、D 都在文中没有出现，而且第一段还提到家人的担心没有成真。

p: A restaurant in the city now sells its unsold dishes at half price after nine at night. The owner says he would throw them away otherwise.
Some customers wait until nine on purpose. Others say they would never eat so late.
Either way, less food ends up in the bin than before.
q: Why does the restaurant sell dishes at half price?
o: To attract more customers at noon.
To avoid throwing the food away.
ex: 第一段 The owner says he would throw them away otherwise（否则就要扔掉），选 B。A 项的「中午」与原文九点之后相反。

p: Working from home saves the time spent on the road. For a worker in a big city that can be two hours a day.
But many people find that the working day has no end. The computer is always there, so they answer messages at midnight.
The advice is to keep a fixed finishing time, just as if you had to catch a bus.
q: What problem do home workers often have?
o: They have no clear end to the working day.
ex: 第二段 the working day has no end ... they answer messages at midnight，选 C。A、B 两项文中都没有依据。

p: Noise in cities comes from many sources, but the one people mention most is traffic. It is not only the engines but also the horns.
Long exposure to traffic noise has been linked to poor sleep and higher stress. Some cities have started to cover busy roads with grass and trees.
The plants absorb part of the sound, and the road looks better too.
q: What have some cities done about traffic noise?
o: Covered busy roads with grass and trees.
ex: 最后一段 Some cities have started to cover busy roads with grass and trees，选 B。A 项文中没有提到「完全禁止鸣笛」。

p: Exercise is often recommended for the body, but its effect on mood is just as important. Thirty minutes of walking can lift a low mood for several hours.
The effect does not depend on how hard you exercise. Even a slow walk in a park counts.
What matters most is that you do it on the day you feel worst.
q: According to the passage, what matters most?
o: Exercising on the day you feel worst.
ex: 最后一句 What matters most is that you do it on the day you feel worst，选 B。第二段还明确说效果与强度无关，排除 A。

p: Computer programs can now translate a page of English into Chinese in a second. The result is usually understandable but not elegant.
Translators still disagree about whether this will replace human translation. What they agree on is that it has changed the job.
Today, human translators spend more time correcting machines than writing from scratch.
q: How has machine translation changed translators' work?
o: They have less work than before.
They spend more time correcting machines.
ex: 最后一句 human translators spend more time correcting machines than writing from scratch，选 B。D 项与原文恰好相反。

p: A teacher in a village school asked her students to teach one topic each to the class. She gave them a week to prepare.
The students were nervous at first, but they read more carefully than usual because they had to explain it. Several of them asked to teach a second topic.
The teacher said she had never seen them work so hard.
q: Why did the students read more carefully?
o: Because they had to explain the topic.
ex: 第二段 they read more carefully than usual because they had to explain it，选 B。

p: Second hand shops used to be for people who could not afford new things. Today many young people shop there by choice.
The reason is partly money and partly the environment. Making a new shirt uses a great deal of water and energy.
Some shops even repair old clothes before selling them.
q: Why do many young people buy second hand clothes today?
o: Because of money and the environment.
ex: 第二段 The reason is partly money and partly the environment（一半为了省钱，一半为了环保），选 B。

p: In one apartment building, the neighbours started a small shelf near the lift. People put books there that they had finished.
At first there were only five books. Within a year the shelf was full, and people began leaving notes inside the covers.
One note said simply: I read this on a rainy Sunday, and it helped.
q: What happened within a year?
o: The shelf became full of books.
ex: 第二段 Within a year the shelf was full，选 B。文中还提到人们在书里留纸条，说明不是「没人读了」。

p: If you review new words the next day, you forget far fewer of them. If you wait a week, most are already gone.
This pattern is called the forgetting curve. It is why teachers tell you to look at yesterday's lesson before starting today's.
The gaps can grow: one day, three days, a week, and then a month.
q: What does the forgetting curve explain?
o: Why reviewing soon after learning helps.
ex: 第二段用曲线解释 It is why teachers tell you to look at yesterday's lesson before starting today's，核心是「早复习有用」，选 B。

p: Most meetings could be an email. That is the opinion of many workers, and the research is on their side.
A short written note forces people to organise their thoughts. A meeting lets the loudest person talk the longest.
Some companies now hold meetings only when a decision has to be made together.
q: What do some companies now do?
o: Hold meetings only for joint decisions.
ex: 最后一句 hold meetings only when a decision has to be made together（只有需要一起做决定时才开会），选 B。C 项「禁止一切会议」过于绝对。

p: Small habits are easier to keep than big plans. Ten minutes of reading a day is more useful than three hours once a month.
The same is true of most things: a short walk, a few new words, a phone call to family.
The hard part is not the size. It is doing it again tomorrow.
q: What does the writer say is the hard part?
o: Doing it again the next day.
ex: 最后一句 The hard part is not the size. It is doing it again tomorrow，选 B。A 项是作者明确排除的。

p: Slow travel means staying in one place for a week or more instead of visiting five cities in five days.
Travellers who try it say they see less but understand more. They start to recognise the shopkeeper and the bus driver.
It is also usually cheaper, because weekly rents are lower than daily ones.
q: What do slow travellers say about their trips?
o: They see less but understand more.
ex: 第二段 they see less but understand more，选 B。C 项与最后一句「通常更便宜」相反。

p: A password that is easy to remember is usually easy to guess. Names, birthdays and simple words are tried first by any attacker.
The safest passwords are long and use three unrelated words. Length matters more than strange symbols.
Writing them down in a notebook at home is safer than using the same one everywhere.
q: According to the passage, what makes a password safest?
ex: 第二段 The safest passwords are long and use three unrelated words. Length matters more than strange symbols，选 A。B 项正是被「长度更重要」否掉的那个。

p: It is natural to compare yourself with classmates, but the comparison is rarely fair. You see their results, not their hours.
A better habit is to compare with your own record from a month ago. That comparison is accurate and it points in a useful direction.
Progress you can measure is easier to trust than progress you can only feel.
q: What does the writer suggest comparing?
o: Your results with your own past results.
ex: 第二段 A better habit is to compare with your own record from a month ago，选 B。A 项正是作者说「不公平」的做法。

p: In many countries, the quality of a school still depends on the postcode of the family. Schools in richer areas have more teachers, more equipment and smaller classes.

Governments have tried several solutions. One is to send the best teachers to weaker schools for a few years, with extra pay and a promise of promotion. Another is to give parents money for after-school classes.
Neither solution works alone. The strongest results appear when teachers are supported inside the school itself, rather than being sent there and left to manage.
q: What does the passage suggest works best?
ex: 第三段 Neither solution works alone ... supported inside the school itself（单靠哪一种都不行，效果最好的是在校内得到支持）说明「支持」是关键条件，选 B。A 项丢掉了 supported 这个限定，恰恰是作者反对的做法。

p: Cities grow because people come for work. The same growth that creates jobs also pushes up rents, and those who came first are often pushed out later.

Some planners argue that building more housing is the only real answer, because prices follow supply. Others point out that new flats are usually sold to investors rather than to the people who need them.
The disagreement is not about numbers but about who counts as a resident.
q: What is the disagreement really about?
ex: 最后一句 The disagreement is not about numbers but about who counts as a resident，作者自己把争论的实质说了出来，选 B。A 项正是作者说「不是重点」的那一项。

p: Every time a notification appears, the brain switches tasks. The switch itself costs only a few seconds, but it takes much longer to return to the same depth of thought.
People who check their phones often are therefore not just losing the seconds of looking. They are losing the deep work that only begins after several quiet minutes.
This is why some people now leave their phones in a drawer while writing.
q: Why is a notification more costly than it appears?
o: It prevents deep work, which needs quiet minutes.
ex: 第二段 They are losing the deep work that only begins after several quiet minutes（丢掉的是要好几分钟安静才进入的深度状态），选 B。A、D 项文中没有依据。

p: Charging drivers to enter the city centre has reduced traffic in several European cities. The number of cars fell within months, and the money was used to improve buses.
The measure is unpopular at first but becomes accepted once people see the buses improve. The political risk is concentrated in the first year.
Cities that abandoned the charge early rarely brought it back.
q: According to the passage, what happens to the charge over time?
ex: 第二段 The measure is unpopular at first but becomes accepted once people see the buses improve，选 B。C 项只对「早早放弃的那批城市」成立，是对原文的扩大化。

p: A survey asked workers what they valued most in a manager. The top answer was not knowledge or experience but predictability.
People said they could work well under a manager who was strict, as long as that manager was consistently strict. What broke morale was not severity but sudden changes in mood.
The lesson is uncomfortable for those who believe being nice matters more than being even.
q: What did the survey find workers valued most?
ex: 第一段 The top answer was not knowledge or experience but predictability，第二段又补充「严但一贯」也能接受，核心是「可预期」，选 C。B 项正是被排除的那个答案。

p: Long working hours are often defended as a sign of commitment. The evidence does not support this.
Studies of people in the same job find that output stops rising after about fifty hours a week, and actually falls after sixty. The extra hours are spent correcting mistakes made when tired.
The problem is that the mistakes are rarely visible on the same day.
q: Why can the harm of long hours go unnoticed?
o: Because the mistakes appear later, not the same day.
ex: 最后一句 the mistakes are rarely visible on the same day（错误很少当天就显现），所以危害不易被察觉，选 B。第三段还提到输出在六十小时后实际下降，排除 D。

p: Advertising rarely tries to argue that a product is good. It is far more effective to suggest that people like you already own it.
This works because the need being sold is not for the object but for belonging. The object is only the ticket.
Understanding this does not make a person immune. It only makes the moment of buying easier to notice.
q: According to the passage, what need does advertising really sell?
ex: 第二段 the need being sold is not for the object but for belonging，选 B。A 项正是作者特意否定的那个。

p: Half of the world's languages may disappear within a century. Most of them are spoken by small groups and have no written form.
When a language dies, more is lost than a set of words. Local knowledge about plants, weather and medicine is stored in the language itself, and much of it is never written down elsewhere.
Recording a language is urgent, but a recording is not the same as a speaker.
q: According to the passage, why does a disappearing language matter?
o: It carries knowledge found nowhere else.
It is spoken by few people.
ex: 第二段 Local knowledge ... is stored in the language itself, and much of it is never written down elsewhere，选 B。C、D 项是客观事实，但它们解释的是「为什么它脆弱」，不是「为什么它值得保护」。

p: Social platforms show people the most successful moments of each other's lives. Nobody posts the boring Tuesday afternoon.
Heavy users therefore compare their ordinary days with a collection of highlights. The result is a feeling of falling behind that has no basis in fact.
The platforms know this. Content that produces strong feelings keeps people on the screen longer.
q: What is the cause of the feeling described?
o: Comparing real life with selected highlights.
ex: 第二段 compare their ordinary days with a collection of highlights. The result is a feeling...（拿普通日子和精选片段比，于是产生这种感觉），选 B。

p: An ageing population is usually described as a problem of cost. That framing hides something important.
Older people also provide a great deal of unpaid work: looking after grandchildren, caring for a sick partner, running community groups. None of it appears in national accounts.
Ignoring this does not make the cost disappear. It only makes the contribution invisible.
q: What point does the writer make?
o: Old people's unpaid work is left out of the picture.
Ageing is not a real issue.
Communities do not need old people.
ex: 第二段列举祖辈看孩子、照顾生病伴侣、组织社区活动等无偿劳动，第三段说 It only makes the contribution invisible，选 B。C 项过于极端，作者只是要求把这部分算进去。

p: Making roads wider to solve traffic jams has been tried for decades. It works for about two years.
After that, the extra space is filled by drivers who previously avoided the route or took the train. The new capacity creates the very demand it was meant to meet.
Cities that build instead of managing are on a treadmill.
q: Why does widening roads stop working after a while?
o: Because the extra capacity attracts new drivers.
ex: 第二段 the extra space is filled by drivers who previously avoided the route（多出来的路面被原本绕行或坐地铁的人填满），选 B。A 项文中没有讨论造价。

p: What a family eats is rarely decided by taste alone. It marks who they are, where they came from and what they are willing to spend.
When people move to another country, the food of home often becomes more important than it ever was before. A dish that was ordinary at home becomes a link back.
This explains why the smell of a market can make someone homesick more than a photograph.
q: Why does the food of home become more important after moving away?
o: Because it becomes a link back to home.
Because there is no other food.
ex: 第二段 A dish that was ordinary at home becomes a link back，选 B。A 项文中没有讨论口味变化。

p: Sleep is not a single state but a cycle of stages. Deep sleep helps the body repair itself, while another stage is where memories are sorted and stored.
Cutting sleep short does not simply remove the extra hours at the end of the night. It removes whichever stage was due next, and the order is not fixed.
That is why the same shortage of sleep affects people differently.
q: Why does the same amount of lost sleep affect people differently?
o: Because different sleep stages are missing.
Because sleep is a single state.
ex: 第二段 It removes whichever stage was due next, and the order is not fixed，第三段 That is why the same shortage ... affects people differently，选 B。D 项与第一段「睡眠不是一个单一状态」矛盾。

p: Putting tablets into classrooms was once treated as a cure for weak teaching. The results have been mixed.
Where the device replaced a poor textbook, students improved. Where it simply sat alongside the old lessons, it added a distraction without adding understanding.
The lesson seems to be that technology multiplies whatever teaching is already there.
q: What is the main conclusion of the passage?
o: Technology strengthens existing teaching, good or bad.
ex: 最后一段 technology multiplies whatever teaching is already there（技术只是把已有的教学质量放大），既能放大好的也能放大差的，选 B。A、C 两项都过于绝对。

p: Cities are warmer than the countryside around them, sometimes by five degrees at night. The concrete stores heat during the day and releases it slowly after dark.
Planting trees helps, but only where they are allowed to grow tall. Short ornamental trees in narrow boxes give shade for an hour and nothing more.
The difference between the two is not money but patience.
q: Why do short ornamental trees help little?
o: They cannot grow tall enough to give real shade.
ex: 第二段 Short ornamental trees in narrow boxes give shade for an hour and nothing more，与「要长成高树才有用」形成对比，选 B。最后一句把差别归到 patience，说明不是钱的问题，排除 A。

p: People say they care about privacy, and they do. But when a free service asks for their location, most of them agree within seconds.
The reason is not ignorance. Agreeing is easy and immediate, while the harm is uncertain and in the future. Behaviour follows what is close, not what is important.
Designers who understand this put the question on the second screen, not the first.
q: Why do most people agree so quickly?
o: They do not care about privacy.
Immediate convenience outweighs a future, uncertain risk.
They do not understand the question.
ex: 第二段 Agreeing is easy and immediate, while the harm is uncertain and in the future. Behaviour follows what is close，选 B。A 项被第一段 they do care 直接否定。

p: A community that organises everything from above tends to stop working when the organiser leaves. One that grows from small groups survives the loss of any individual.
The reason is not sentiment but structure. Many small groups fail separately and safely; one large group fails all at once.
This is why experienced community workers start with a single street.
q: Why do experienced community workers start small?
o: Because many small groups fail separately and safely.
ex: 第二段 Many small groups fail separately and safely; one large group fails all at once，选 B。

p: A little pressure improves performance. Too much destroys it. The interesting question is where the line lies.
Research suggests the line depends less on the amount of work than on whether the person believes they control it. The same task given as a choice is far less stressful.
Control, not volume, is what separates pressure from distress.
q: According to the passage, what makes pressure harmful?
ex: 第二段 depends less on the amount of work than on whether the person believes they control it，第三段又总结 Control, not volume, is what separates pressure from distress，选 B。A 项正是被排除的那个。

p: Reading on a screen encourages skimming. The eye moves quickly down the page, looking for something useful.
This is efficient for finding a fact and poor for following an argument, which only reveals itself across several paragraphs. The reader arrives at the end with no idea what was claimed.
The medium does not decide the outcome, but it does set a default.
q: What is the problem with skimming?
o: Arguments unfold across paragraphs and are missed.
ex: 第二段 poor for following an argument, which only reveals itself across several paragraphs，选 B。A 项与第一段「眼睛移动很快」相反。

p: A shirt that costs less than a meal is cheap only because the cost was moved somewhere else. It was moved to the wages of the person who sewed it and to the river that received the dye.
Consumers are not usually told any of this. What they see is the price tag, which is the only part of the story that fits on a label.
Campaigns that demand cheaper clothes therefore argue against their own aim.
q: What point does the writer make about demanding cheaper clothes?
o: It is the best way to help workers.
It works against the goal of fair pay.
It has no effect at all.
ex: 最后一句 Campaigns that demand cheaper clothes therefore argue against their own aim（要求衣服更便宜的运动其实与自己的目标相悖），选 B。

p: A square with benches will be used by old people in the morning and by teenagers in the evening. A square without benches is used by neither.
The design detail looks trivial and is not. Seats decide who is welcome, and they cost almost nothing compared with paving or lighting.
Cities that want lively public space usually get the small things right first.
q: Why are benches important?
o: They cost a lot of money.
They decide who is welcome to stay.
ex: 第二段 Seats decide who is welcome，选 B。A 项与原文 almost nothing compared with paving 相反。

p: Beginners improve quickly, which makes practice feel rewarding. The improvement then slows, and the same amount of effort produces much less visible change.
This is the point at which most learners stop. They conclude that they have reached their limit, when in fact the learning has simply become harder to see.
Knowing this in advance is the best protection against quitting.
q: Why do most learners stop?
o: They mistake slower visible progress for a limit.
They lose interest in the subject.
ex: 第二段 They conclude that they have reached their limit, when in fact the learning has simply become harder to see，选 B。C 项「失去兴趣」是结果，不是作者给出的原因。

p: Remote work removes the office but not the need for other people. Most people who work from home still want somewhere to go once or twice a week.
What they are looking for is not the desk but the accidental conversation. It is hard to plan and easy to notice when it is missing.
This is why the firms that cut their offices entirely are often the first to rent small ones again.
q: What do home workers miss most?
ex: 第二段 What they are looking for is not the desk but the accidental conversation，选 B。A 项正是被排除的。

p: Recycling is presented as the answer to plastic waste, and it is used to justify producing more of it.
In practice only a small share of plastic is ever recycled, and each cycle produces a lower quality material. A bottle can become a bottle once or twice, then nothing.
Reducing the amount produced is less satisfying than recycling, and far more effective.
q: What is the writer's view of recycling?
o: It is useful but cannot justify producing more.
It produces better material each time.
ex: 第一段 it is used to justify producing more（回收被用来为增产背书），第三段又说减少产量 far more effective，可见作者认为回收有用但不能当作增产的理由，选 B。C 项与原文不符，作者并未主张停止回收。

p: Tourism often turns a local festival into a performance for visitors. The date moves to suit the holiday season and the ceremony is shortened.
Something real is gained: the town earns money and the craft survives. Something is lost: the event now happens for the audience rather than for the community.
Both effects are true at once, which is why the arguments never end.
q: Why do the arguments about tourism never end?
o: Because real gains and real losses happen together.
ex: 第三段 Both effects are true at once, which is why the arguments never end，选 B。

p: Automation removes tasks rather than whole jobs. A bank clerk who no longer counts cash still has customers to deal with.
The difficulty is that the removed tasks are often the easy, relaxing ones, while what remains is the stressful part. The job survives in a harder form.
This is why workers often resist a change that looks harmless from outside.
q: Why do workers resist some forms of automation?
o: Because the tasks left behind are the harder ones.
ex: 第二段 the removed tasks are often the easy, relaxing ones, while what remains is the stressful part，选 B。A 项与第一段「自动化拿走的是任务而不是整个工作」矛盾。

p: A to-do list with twenty items is not a plan. It is a way of feeling busy while avoiding the decision about what matters.
The useful exercise is to cross out half the list before starting. What remains is usually longer work and less comfortable, which is exactly why it was being avoided.
A short list is harder to write than a long one.
q: What does the writer suggest doing with a long to-do list?
o: Crossing out half of it first.
ex: 第二段 The useful exercise is to cross out half the list before starting，选 B。

p: Every new communication tool has been blamed for making people ruder. The telephone, the short message and the social feed were each accused of the same thing.
What actually changed is not politeness but the cost of interrupting. A letter waited on a desk for a day. A message arrives now, and the person expects an answer.
The rudeness people notice is usually the price of that speed.
q: What does the writer say actually changed?
ex: 第二段 What actually changed is not politeness but the cost of interrupting（真正变的不是礼貌，而是打断别人的代价），选 B。A 项被同一句话直接否定。

p: People who believe ability is fixed treat failure as information about themselves. People who believe ability can grow treat the same failure as information about the task.
The second group recovers faster, and not because they are braver. They simply have somewhere else to put the result.
The belief is not a trick. It is what makes the next attempt possible at all.
q: Why do people who believe ability can grow recover faster?
o: They treat failure as information about the task.
ex: 第一段 People who believe ability can grow treat the same failure as information about the task，选 B。A 项被第二段 not because they are braver 明确排除。
